# Introduction

The Orthologous MAtrix (OMA) project is a method and database for the
inference of orthologs among complete genomes
([omabrowser.org](https://omabrowser.org)). The OMA Browser provides several
types of orthology predictions for thousands of genomes across the tree of
life:

- pairwise orthologs between proteins of two genomes,
- OMA Groups, i.e. groups of proteins that are all orthologous to each
    other, and
- Hierarchical Orthologous Groups (HOGs), i.e. groups of genes that
    descended from a single ancestral gene at a given taxonomic level.

`OmaDB` gives access to the data of the OMA Browser from R, using its REST
API. It returns the data as data.frames and objects using standard
Bioconductor classes (e.g. `GRanges`, `AAString`), so that it can be
directly used in downstream analyses. A similar package exists for Python
([pyomadb](https://github.com/DessimozLab/pyomadb)). Other Bioconductor
packages provide orthology information for a limited set of model
organisms (e.g. the `Orthology.eg.db` annotation package) or gene trees
from other resources (e.g. `biomaRt` for Ensembl Compara), while `OmaDB`
covers all genomes in OMA and gives access to the hierarchical orthologous
groups and the ancestral genomes inferred by OMA.

As `OmaDB` queries the OMA Browser, it requires an internet connection.

This vignette gives an overview of the package. More details are given in
the vignettes on HOGs, the taxonomy and sequence analyses.

# Installation

`OmaDB` is available from Bioconductor and can be installed as follows:

```{r install, eval = FALSE}
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) {
    install.packages("BiocManager")
}
BiocManager::install("OmaDB")
```

```{r load, message = FALSE}
library(OmaDB)
```

# Overview of the package

The functions of the package correspond to the main entities of the OMA
Browser:

| Function | Retrieves |
|---|---|
| `getProtein()` | proteins, their orthologs, GO annotations, ... |
| `searchProtein()` | proteins matching an identifier |
| `mapSequence()` | proteins matching a sequence |
| `getOMAGroup()` | OMA Groups |
| `getHOG()`, `getHOGs()`, `getOrthoXML()` | Hierarchical Orthologous Groups |
| `getGenome()` | genomes and their proteins |
| `getGenomePairs()`, `getSharedAncestry()` | orthologs between two genomes |
| `getTaxonomy()` | the taxonomy of the genomes |
| `getSynteny()` | (ancestral) gene order |
| `annotateSequence()` | predicted GO annotations for a sequence |

The results follow simple rules: an entity (e.g. a protein or a genome) is
returned as an object of class `omadb_obj`, a list of entities (e.g. the
orthologs of a protein) is returned as a data.frame.

```{r version}
getVersion()
```

# Proteins

Proteins can be retrieved with any unique identifier, e.g. a UniProtKB
accession, an OMA id or a RefSeq id. If an identifier is not unique,
`searchProtein()` lists all matching proteins.

```{r search}
hits <- searchProtein("P53_HUMAN")
hits[, c("xref", "source", "omaid")]
```

```{r protein}
p53 <- getProtein("P53_HUMAN")
p53
```

The protein sequence is an `AAString` and the genomic locus a `GRanges`
object:

```{r protein-attributes}
p53$sequence
p53$locus
```

Some attributes, such as the orthologs or the GO annotations, are loaded
from the OMA Browser when they are accessed (they are shown as
`<loaded on access>` above):

```{r lazy}
orthologs <- p53$orthologs
dim(orthologs)
head(orthologs[, c("omaid", "species.species", "rel_type")])
table(orthologs$rel_type)
```

The same data can be retrieved directly with the `attribute` argument,
also for several proteins at once. For several proteins, the column
`query_id` contains the queried identifier:

```{r attribute}
go <- getProtein(c("P53_HUMAN", "P53_MOUSE"), attribute = "gene_ontology")
head(go[, c("query_id", "GO_term", "name", "aspect")])
```

The function `getObjectAttributes()` lists the attributes of an object and
`as.data.frame()` converts it into a data.frame with a single row:

```{r as-data-frame}
head(getObjectAttributes(p53))
df <- as.data.frame(p53)
df[, c("omaid", "canonicalid", "species.code", "oma_group")]
```

# OMA Groups

OMA Groups are cliques of proteins that are all orthologous to each other.
As they contain at most one protein per species, they are often used as
marker genes for phylogenetic analyses.

```{r group}
group <- getOMAGroup(p53$oma_group)
group$fingerprint
nrow(group$members)
head(group$members[, c("omaid", "canonicalid", "species.species")])
```

`getLocus()` converts the loci of a set of proteins into a `GRanges`
object:

```{r locus}
getLocus(head(group$members, 5))
```

# Genomes and their orthologs

`getGenome()` lists all genomes in the OMA Browser or retrieves a single
genome.

```{r genome}
genome <- getGenome("ASHGO")
genome$species
genome$chromosomes
```

The orthologs between two genomes can be retrieved with `getGenomePairs()`,
optionally restricted to certain chromosomes and types of orthology.
`getSharedAncestry()` summarises the number of orthologs between two
genomes.

```{r pairs}
pairs <- getGenomePairs("YEAST", "ASHGO", chr2 = "I")
table(pairs$rel_type)
head(pairs[, c("entry_1.omaid", "entry_2.omaid", "rel_type")])
getSharedAncestry("YEAST", "ASHGO")$details
```

# Caching

All responses of the OMA Browser are cached in memory, so repeated queries
are fast and do not burden the server. The cache can also be stored on
disk to reuse it across R sessions. It is cleared automatically when a new
release of the OMA Browser is available.

```{r cache, eval = FALSE}
setOmaCache(persistent = TRUE)
```

The OMA Browser REST API is documented at
<https://omabrowser.org/api/docs>.

# Session information

```{r session-info}
sessionInfo()
```
